request.prompt: Instrumental game soundtrack loop for a 2D pixel-art platformer: a child explores a storybook Persian castle that has become a school-prison dungeon of locked cages, keys and stone wings. Mysterious and curious rather than scary, playful tension. Plucked tar and setar ostinato, soft daf frame drum pulse, low bowed kamancheh drone, distant santur glints, echoing stone-hall space. Medium-slow tempo around 90 BPM, steady pulse, minor Persian Shur colour. Consistent energy throughout with no big intro, breakdown or ending, so it loops cleanly. No vocals.

alternates.source/darkshang_theme_taiko_v1.mp3: Instrumental Persian chase music for a dark platformer pursuit, built around percussion. Lead percussion is a Persian tombak goblet drum played with fast virtuosic finger rolls, deep bass 'tom' strokes and sharp rim 'bak' clicks, answered by a darbuka (doumbek) playing a driving maqsum dum-tek-tek-dum-tek rhythm, with a large frame daf and riq jingles on the off-beats. Over the drums, a tense kamancheh spike fiddle and a breathy ney flute trade short ominous phrases in Persian dastgah Homayun with its augmented second, plucked tar ostinato underneath, a low drone. Urgent, relentless, dark and mysterious, around 120 BPM, consistent high intensity the whole way with no intro, no breakdown and no ending so it loops seamlessly. No Western orchestra, no taiko, no synths, no vocals.

A low santur tremolo ostinato and a gritty tar riff in Persian Chahargah mode, with a mournful kamancheh and ney answering on top. Ominous, urgent, a shadow is chasing you through a moonlit city at night. Around 126 BPM, constant intensity from start to finish with no intro, breakdown or ending so it loops seamlessly. Acoustic instruments only: no taiko, no orchestral strings, no synths, no vocals.

request.prompt: Instrumental title-screen theme for a 2D pixel-art platformer about Hooshang, an elderly Iranian office worker who escapes a dark corporate office and rediscovers the warmth of his childhood in Iran, guided by the poet Rumi. Warm, nostalgic and hopeful, bittersweet but never eerie, dark or scary. A breathy ney reed flute carries a simple, memorable, singable melody in Persian Dashti colour (from dastgah Shur), over gently rolling santur arpeggios and soft setar plucks, with a warm low string pad underneath. Only a few soft daf frame-drum touches, no driving percussion and no tombak. Slow, calm, unhurried tempo around 76 BPM, steady pulse. Consistent energy throughout with no big intro, build, breakdown or ending, so it loops cleanly. No vocals.

Instrumental cinematic action chase cue for a 2D pixel-art platformer: a tiger is hunting an old man through a forest and over cliff-top rocks, always one breath behind him. Primal, ferocious, relentless and breathless: you are prey running for your life. Persian war-drum fury meets epic film score: thundering low dohol and huge frame drums pounding like a big cat's paws in a fast galloping 6/8, rapid tombak rolls and finger strikes, a string section and kamancheh sawing fierce fast ostinatos, a tar strummed hard and aggressive, low brass snarling on the off-beats like a growl, and piercing ney shrieks at the ends of phrases. Persian dastgah Homayoun, dark and urgent. Fast, around 152 BPM. It opens instantly at full intensity on one huge drum-and-low-brass hit, with no fade-in and no slow build, then holds that relentless driving intensity for the whole length with no breakdown, no quiet passage and no ending, so it loops cleanly. No vocals.

Instrumental cinematic score for the moment an old Iranian man, after a long dark journey under the sea, walks out of his office at dawn and stands barefoot in the real sea at sunrise. Overwhelming quiet joy and release, tender and luminous, tears of relief: the first real daylight in the whole game. A breathy ney reed flute sings a long, simple, singable homecoming melody in Persian Dashti colour (from dastgah Shur), over shimmering santur arpeggios like sunlight glittering on water, a slow-blooming warm string orchestra, soft sustained horns and a low warm pad, with gentle swells like waves. No drums except a few soft, distant daf touches. Slow, around 66 BPM, spacious and unhurried. It begins with a slow warm swell rising out of silence over the first few seconds, then settles into the melody at a steady, glowing level. After that opening, consistent energy with no further build, breakdown or ending, so it loops cleanly. No vocals.

Instrumental walking theme for a 2D pixel-art platformer: an elderly Iranian man walks home along a sunny shore road and up into a high meadow of poppies above the sea, free at last, with nothing chasing him. Light, unhurried, content and quietly happy, a gentle morning stroll in sunlight and sea breeze; pastoral but never childish or cartoonish. A setar plucks a lilting, memorable Persian folk melody in dastgah Mahur, answered by a warm kamancheh countermelody; light pizzicato strings and soft santur keep a walking pulse; a gentle daf and tombak play a relaxed, swaying groove; now and then a bright ney flourish like birdsong. Walking tempo around 92 BPM, steady pulse. Consistent energy throughout with no big intro, build, breakdown or ending, so it loops cleanly. No vocals.

Instrumental suspense underscore for a 2D game: walking into tall grass where the wind has suddenly stopped and something unseen is watching from very close. Still, airless and uneasy, quiet but full of dread: a predator stalking. Sustained high string harmonics over a cold low string drone, a single low setar note plucked every few seconds with long silence around it, breathy ney air with no melody, soft rustling textures, and a slow, faint, distant frame-drum heartbeat. Persian dastgah Homayoun colour. Almost no rhythm, very sparse, around 60 BPM, low volume throughout, never building to a climax. Consistent energy throughout with no big intro, build, breakdown or ending, so it loops cleanly. No vocals.

Instrumental underscore for a frozen moment of peril: an old man hangs from a single vine on a cliff face, a hungry tiger waiting above and another pacing below, while two mice slowly gnaw through the vine. Suspended, quiet and tense, yet strangely still, as if time has stopped. A very low sustained cello and double-bass drone, a slow, soft heartbeat on a low frame drum, a dry, steady high pizzicato tick like a clock, faint airy ney breaths and a distant cold string harmonic. Persian dastgah Homayoun colour. Slow, around 60 BPM, very sparse and restrained, low volume, no real melody and no climax. Consistent energy throughout with no big intro, build, breakdown or ending, so it loops cleanly. No vocals.

Instrumental finale for the last moment of a game: an old man hanging from a vine between two tigers picks a lemon growing from the cliff, tastes it, and for the first time in his life is completely present. Tender, sweet, grateful and quietly radiant: peace in the middle of danger, the end of the whole story. It begins from near silence with a solo breathy ney reed flute singing a simple, aching homecoming melody in Persian Dashti colour (from dastgah Shur). After about fifteen seconds a gentle santur joins with soft rolling arpeggios, then a setar. After about forty seconds a warm string orchestra blooms underneath and the melody rises to a full, heartfelt, glowing climax around the one-minute mark, never loud or bombastic. Then everything thins back down to the ney and santur alone, and the piece ends on a long, peaceful held note that fades to silence. Slow and rubato, around 64 BPM. No percussion except a few very soft daf touches near the climax. No vocals.

Instrumental cinematic action chase cue for a 2D pixel-art platformer: a tiger is hunting an old man through a forest and over cliff-top rocks, always one breath behind him. Driven above all by DRUMS: massive low dohol and big frame drums hammering a galloping 6/8 rhythm like a charging tiger's paws, deep booming hits on every downbeat, rapid tombak rolls and stomping low toms; a heavy low cello and double-bass ostinato and growling low brass underneath; kamancheh and tar slashing fast Persian phrases on top; short piercing ney shrieks. Dark, heavy, ferocious and primal, low and powerful rather than bright: you are prey running for your life. Persian dastgah Homayoun. Fast, around 152 BPM. It opens instantly at full intensity on one huge drum-and-low-brass hit, with no fade-in and no slow build, then holds that relentless driving intensity for the whole length with no breakdown, no quiet passage and no ending, so it loops cleanly. No vocals.
